text:
An angel descended to Pindus one day,

for him a muse of love sighed;

you were born, oh beautiful one, of that harmony.

Her inspired brow, her ambrosial voice,

the Muse gave you.


She gave you, as mother, her enchanting form,

her nymph's step, her plaint of love,

her moon eyes and gentle hair;

while the angel, from celestial sphere,

gave you radiance.


A song of joy sounded on Olympus,

then heaven sorrowfully moaned;

the former joyfully acquired a virgin,

heaven lost a beloved angel

and the world applauded.


And you before the applause, incautious, ah! forget

that God formed the angel for heaven.

I weep illusions, how sadly lost,

seeing your wings already sold to the world...

An angel, you?... No longer.

translation.title: An Angel Descended to Pindus One Day...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the mythological register and the poem's final disillusionment.
